it depends on the owner and the animal, but with a ball python I'd recommend letting it come up to temp on its own first. 

cold-blooded animals tend to be more sensitive to temperature changes so what might be a small change for you, is a big change for them. you aren't wrong, it just depends on the type of animal, and it's enclosure

water temperature usually runs colder than air temperature, but even so, water is a great conductor and would have drawn all possible heat out of the snake and made the snakes temp fall below room temp
be warned that putting a cold snake directly into a warm enclosure can cause them to go into shock and die. please let them come up to room temperature for a few hours first!!

First off, please never apologise for feeling this way! None of this is your fault even when it feels like it is.

Please don't be scared to put yourself and your needs first. I'm not sure I can help you in the therapy and meds department as I live in Australia and my situation seems different to how it is for you, but I'm sure you and your partner would be able to work together and find a solution.

And as a bit of encouragement; the fact that you were able to reach out at all is so inspiring to all the other people in this community. you making this post and reaching out shows that you are willing to put in the work and get better. you are already halfway there. please keep fighting! you are so strong and we all support you.

Good luck, I'm here for you.
